title: jwn contract
description: Every document the daemon and a client exchange. Entry points: ClientMsg, DaemonMsg. Unknown properties are allowed everywhere on purpose (additive changes never break an old peer).

Inline.description: A run of text with one style.

MdBlock.description: A piece of a Markdown document, as read_markdown replies and a finished text of a conversation carries.

Item.description: One thing in a conversation, oldest first.

Color.description: A palette index (0 to 255) or a #rrggbb string.

AgentEvent.description: The hooks of an agent the daemon listens to.

DiffScope.description: What a diff compares: the working tree with HEAD, this branch with its merge base with origin's default branch, or one commit with its first parent.

DiffState.description: no_base: origin has no default branch, so a general diff has nothing to compare with.

Seen.description: yes: looked at and unchanged since; changed: looked at, but the file differs now.

context.description: The text git prints after the second @@ (usually the enclosing function).

lines.description: Each line prefixed with + (added), - (deleted) or a space (unchanged).

unreadable.description: Why the daemon did not read the file: symlink, too_big.

base.description: What general compares with, such as origin/main.

omitted.description: Files left out of a too large diff.

older.description: The time of the first item: the before of read_older.

held.description: Another claude that has this session open.

cwd.description: The folder the engine runs in: the folder its @ references are written from.

suggestion.description: What Claude proposes the person writes next.

following.description: When the turn began that another claude runs in the transcript this conversation follows.

tokens.description: What the turn that runs has written.

TextDoc.description: What read_file replies: a text file as lines of runs; k is the syntax class (kw, str, num, ty, fn, cm, attr) and a reader shows an unknown or missing one as plain text.

Denied.description: Why the bridge refused a phone: the pairing token was wrong, expired or spent; the person at the PC said no or did not answer; the device secret is unknown or revoked; too many failures from this address.

PhoneMsg.description: What a phone sends the bridge before the daemon's protocol starts: it either spends a pairing token or proves a paired device. After `ready` the stream carries ClientMsg.

BridgeMsg.description: What the bridge sends a phone: the answer to pair or auth, then (after `ready`) the addresses the PC can be reached at. After `ready` the stream also carries DaemonMsg.

lan.description: host:port of the TLS listener on the PC's private address

tunnel.description: host name of the Cloudflare tunnel
